clue.text: Ground squirrel's plain tail

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay

parts.note: a prairie is a wide grassy plain
to tail someone is to dog them, following closely

explanation.surface: A note that a ground squirrel has an unremarkable, ordinary tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail' looks like a noun belonging to the squirrel, but it is a verb meaning to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The North American burrowing rodent called a prairie dog belongs to the squirrel family and lives underground.

clue.text: Quick pint following concert

indicators.note: the pint comes after the concert in the answer, so this places it second

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as in the BBC Proms

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a swift drink straight after a gig.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt and quick are synonyms describing something done without delay.

clue.text: Guitarist, American celebrity, turned up after ten

indicators.note: the celebrity part sits after the ten in the answer

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a big name is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A famous American guitarist shows up after ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' suggests arriving, but it reverses NAME to EMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Axe is slang for a guitar, so an axeman is a guitarist, especially in rock.

clue.text: Forcefully reprimanded aide that rector foolishly employed

indicators.note: the letters are arranged foolishly, i.e. in a jumbled new order

explanation.surface: A rector's aide behaved foolishly and was given a stern telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from the Riot Act of 1714, read aloud to disperse crowds; now it means to scold severely.

clue.text: Ad-lib from former European politician in shot

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the European politician sits inside the word for shot

parts.note: shot in the sense of rushed or sped, like tore
MP is Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A former European politician improvises an off-the-cuff remark in a photo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests a photograph, but it is the past tense of shoot, meaning sped, giving TORE around EMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Extempore speech is delivered without preparation, just as an ad-lib is improvised.

clue.text: Ring when computer device fails to start

indicators.note: the device loses its opening letter, so it cannot get started

parts.note: a router is a networking device for computers

explanation.surface: A phone call when your computer gadget won't boot up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests a phone call, but it is the outer ring of an archery target.
explanation.definitionFit: On a target the outer is the outermost ring, and a shot landing there is also called an outer.

clue.text: Old king's unwell, onset of angina

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay

parts.note: feeling off means feeling unwell

indicators.note: onset is the beginning, so only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch falls ill with the first signs of a heart condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, famous for Offa's Dyke on the Welsh border.

clue.text: In which one may see a hooker face controversy

definitions.text: In which one may see a hooker

parts.note: the face is the front
a row is a quarrel or controversy

explanation.surface: A scandal involving a prostitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooker' suggests a prostitute but is the rugby forward who hooks the ball in the scrum's front row.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the hooker is one of three forwards packing down in the scrum's front row.

clue.text: A wild bender across eastern Scottish city

indicators.note: the jumbled letters stretch across the E, enclosing it
the letters run wild and get rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunken spree across the east of Scotland's cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns BENDER into BERDEN, which goes round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a city on the north-east coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Anguish over boundary, reportedly hit very hard and at great speed

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits over the rest

parts.note: hell is torment or anguish

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word heard rather than seen, so the sound counts

parts.note: in cricket a boundary hit along the ground scores four
to leather is to beat or hit hard

explanation.surface: A cricketer in anguish over a boundary, which was struck very hard.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a ball reaching the boundary along the ground scores four runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell for leather is an idiom meaning as fast as possible, originally of horse riding.

clue.text: Love enormous Greek character

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
mega is slang for enormous

explanation.surface: A tremendous love for a Greek person.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: Name character for Othello, say

parts.note: a title is the name of a book or play
a role is a character played by an actor

explanation.surface: Choosing a name for a character such as Othello.
explanation.walkthrough: Othello is the part in Shakespeare's play that shares the play's name; 'say' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A title role is the part whose name the play bears, and Othello is one example.

clue.text: Apparition in seasonal show stealing hearts — Marley's head

indicators.note: the show takes the hearts into itself, holding them inside

parts.note: a panto (pantomime) is the British Christmas-season stage show
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Christmas show steals the emotion with a ghostly Marley, as in A Christmas Carol.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is a British Christmas family theatre tradition. Marley's ghost in A Christmas Carol makes the scene fit the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantom is a ghost or spectre, the same as an apparition.

clue.text: Narrated start of romp filled with happiness

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: elated means full of happiness; the word stands in for that state

explanation.surface: Someone recounted how the beginning of a romp was joyous.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell it, so related is a synonym of narrated.

clue.text: Another heavy weight, individual best

parts.note: a second one is another one
a ton is a large unit of weight
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: Another heavyweight boxer turns out to be the top individual.
explanation.definitionFit: Second to none means unsurpassed, inferior to nobody, which makes it the best.

clue.text: Discourage fellow cleaner

parts.note: to deter is to discourage
a gent is a gentleman or fellow

explanation.surface: Putting off a man who cleans for a living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleaner' reads as a person, but it is a washing product.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a cleaning agent used for washing clothes and dishes.

clue.text: US rock star trashed rooms across Rhode Island — indefinite number

indicators.note: the jumbled letters stretch across the state abbreviation, enclosing it
a trashed room is wrecked, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A rock star wrecks hotel rooms across a US state, a typical rock-and-roll tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface leans on the hard-living image of Jim Morrison of the Doors; 'trashed' and 'across' are the working signals, not hotel damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Jim Morrison was the American singer of the rock band the Doors.

clue.text: TV could show dope case

parts.note: a dope is a fool or idiot
a box is a case or container

explanation.surface: A television programme could expose a drugs case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' and 'case' suggest a drugs investigation, but they are a fool and a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiot box is a slang, disparaging name for a television set.

clue.text: Worn-out elves wait for treatment in fairy story

parts.note: worn-out things are old

indicators.note: the letters are treated, worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Tired elves queue up for medical treatment in a fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: An old wives' tale is a traditional but untrue belief, a fiction like a fairy story.

clue.text: Location surrounding a magnificent residence

indicators.note: the location word goes round the A

parts.note: a place is a location

explanation.surface: A setting enclosing a grand home.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is a grand residence of a monarch or bishop.

clue.text: Dog in street, barking

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go crazy and rearrange

explanation.surface: A dog barking out in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' fits the dog, but here it means mad, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a breed of gun dog, such as the Irish or English setter.

clue.text: List contains duck and crowing bird

indicators.note: the list holds the zero within it

parts.note: a roster is a list of names, like a duty rota
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, written as O

explanation.surface: A list of farm animals includes a duck and a bird that crows.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a male chicken, the bird known for crowing at dawn.

clue.text: Bring up lift

definitions.meaning: to ... children is to bring them up
to ... an object is to lift it

explanation.surface: Bring up lift
explanation.definitionFit: Raise means both to rear a child and to elevate something physically.

clue.text: All are affected by English beer

indicators.note: the letters are affected, altered into a different order

explanation.surface: Everyone is influenced by an English beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' looks like a verb about drinkers, but it signals the rearrangement; Real Ale is a phrase championed by the British Campaign for Real Ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Real ale is the British term for traditional cask-conditioned beer.

clue.text: Endorse editor's assistant and writer

parts.note: a sub is a sub-editor, who helps the editor
a scribe is a writer

explanation.surface: An editor's helper and an author both give their approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To subscribe to a view is to support or endorse it, originally by signing beneath it.

clue.text: Listen to trumpet initially, and organ

parts.note: to hear is to listen to

indicators.note: initially means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Listen to a trumpet and an organ playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the musical instrument, but it is a body organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart is the body organ that pumps blood.

clue.text: Ten falling into trap immediately after

indicators.note: ten drops inside the trap word

parts.note: a net is a trap
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Ten animals fall into a trap one right after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Next means following straight on, coming immediately after.

clue.text: Quite rare, yet growing wild in former times

parts.note: quite! is an exclamation of agreement, like yes

indicators.note: the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A plant that is quite rare yet grows wild, as in the old days.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesteryear means the past, used adverbially for days gone by.
